clue.text: Physio service adheres to European Union rule

parts.note: a mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A physiotherapy practice is said to be following an EU regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adheres to' simply sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio treats the body by manipulation, and someone giving massage professionally is a close equivalent.

clue.text: The smallest skirt mother wanted

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
mum is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother wanted the shortest skirt going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' is only a link joining the pieces into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The least possible amount is the noun for the smallest, as in 'the least you can do'.

clue.text: Even daughter agreed

parts.note: two parties who are even are square

explanation.surface: Even the daughter agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or reconcile something with someone is to square it, so an agreed matter is settled.

clue.text: Cavell, say, handled it heroically, imprisoned within

indicators.note: imprisoned within says the answer is locked inside the words before it

explanation.surface: Nurse Cavell bravely coped while imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed by the Germans in 1915 after helping Allied soldiers escape; the surface draws on her imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the first name of nurse Cavell; 'say' marks her as one example of a person with it.

clue.text: Learns in the course of proper dummy run

indicators.note: in the course of puts one word in the middle of another

parts.note: real means proper or genuine
to hear of something is to learn it

explanation.surface: Someone learns things during a proper trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before the real thing is a trial run of this kind.

clue.text: In good health and not working, so moderately wealthy?

parts.note: someone in good health is well
a machine or worker not working is off

explanation.surface: A healthy person with no job wonders whether that makes them comfortably rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that being healthy and idle doesn't really make you rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably provided with money is the standard sense of this idiom.

clue.text: Movie star — Rooney, for example

definitions.meaning: John ... was a Hollywood film star of westerns
... Rooney is an English footballer, one person with this first name

explanation.definitionFit: John Wayne starred in westerns, and footballer Rooney shares the name as a forename.

clue.text: Boulanger playing in part of hotel, perhaps

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The French music teacher Nadia Boulanger performing in a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: Nadia Boulanger was a celebrated French composer and teacher, which makes 'playing' look musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable drinking room in a hotel or pub, with 'perhaps' because it is found elsewhere too.

clue.text: Material made from angora, woven around back of fez

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged word about the single letter
weaving works threads into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fabric woven from angora wool is wrapped around the back of a fez.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges ANGORA into ORGANA; 'around' puts that about Z, the back of 'fez'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thin stiff sheer fabric, a material used in evening wear.

clue.text: Send on attacking player

definitions.meaning: to send on a letter is to pass it to a new address
in football or rugby an attacker plays in the front line

explanation.definitionFit: Mail is sent on to a new address, and a front-line attacking player bears this position name.

clue.text: Small number of us on island, hard to feed

parts.note: N is the short form of number
something of us is ours, giving the possessive our
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A handful of us marooned on an island find it difficult to get food.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed something is to give it sustenance, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: More inexperienced guy, one out before end of over

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the two words beside it are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cricket report on a novice batsman dismissed just before the over finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GUY and ONE into YOUNGE; the last letter of 'over' adds R. The cricket picture makes 'out' look like a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of fewer years generally means having less experience, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: I joined 14's party to protest before race

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
to hare is to race along

explanation.surface: Someone recalls joining a political party's protest ahead of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 14-down's party is the mad tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, where this character was a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: The character from Lewis Carroll's Wonderland attended the famous tea party, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: Port — sail from one over in Georgia

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: over says the word one is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A travel note about a port where one may sail over from Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sail' is a second definition: a genoa is a large jib used on racing yachts. 'over' turns the number round (ENO) before 'in' sets it inside the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is the major Italian seaport, and a genoa is also a large foresail used on yachts.

clue.text: How one may address a woman from the West or East?

definitions.text: How one may address a woman

indicators.note: reading from the west or east in an across entry means left to right or right to left, and the word is the same both ways

parts.words: How one may address a woman
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A question of polite form when speaking to a lady from either hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal term of respectful address used to a woman, as a shop assistant might.

clue.text: Tea drinker making foolish threat, animatedly

parts.note: mad means foolish

indicators.note: animatedly suggests lively movement that throws the letters about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sipping tea makes a silly threat in a lively manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animatedly' rearranges THREAT into HATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lewis Carroll character hosts an endless tea party, so he is a famous tea drinker.

clue.text: The right side leading table

parts.note: a leading performer is the star
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A description of the righthand end of a top table.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the side on the right when facing forward is called by this nautical name.

clue.text: Excellent naval officer penning book, second in series

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, like an animal in a pen

parts.note: an admiral is a senior naval officer

indicators.note: second in picks the second letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A fine naval officer writing a book, the second in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing B inside ADMIRAL, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserving of admiration is excellent, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Chief to censure bridge contract

parts.note: grand means chief or principal
to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A head of department rebuking a deal over a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a construction contract for a bridge; it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game bridge, bidding to take all thirteen tricks is this contract.

clue.text: (on-line version) Gourmand has good time in Bedfordshire town

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the town name

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A food lover enjoys himself in Luton.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a large town in the English county of Bedfordshire, home to an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a person who eats greedily, which is the sense of this word.

clue.text: An American theatre award going to maiden opposite

parts.note: the Tony is the US award for Broadway theatre
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A Tony award goes to a young woman instead of the opposite candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the opposite meaning to another is the grammar term here, used as a noun.

clue.text: Puzzle over people carrier

parts.note: re means concerning, over as in a dispute over something
a bus carries people

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a family car, a so-called people carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: A people carrier is a British term for a minivan, but here it is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle in which pictures or symbols represent words is this kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Nothing inside three-masted vessel is rococo

indicators.note: inside puts the zero letter within the ship's name

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship usually with three masts
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty three-masted ship decorated in ornate style.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ornate European styles of art and architecture, rococo being the late phase of the other.

clue.text: Spotted guarding ambassador and bishop in drinking den

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding something to protect it

parts.note: something spotted has been seen
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A diplomat and a cleric are seen being escorted in an illicit bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking house, originally in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit Irish or South African bar is this kind of drinking den.

clue.text: Last month leading artist identified as extremist

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Last month a prominent painter was exposed as a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding extreme views, especially politically, is called by this Latin-derived word.

clue.text: Held back playing for second eleven? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a player in a club's second team is in the reserves

explanation.surface: A cricketer is held back to turn out for the second team, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: Second eleven is a cricket or football club's reserve team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept back for later use is said to be kept aside for when needed, the same idea.

clue.text: One politician the Spanish push forward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A politician and some Spanish people urge progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or urge something onward is to push it forward, a synonym.

clue.text: Classifies courts as redundant

indicators.note: being made redundant means losing your place, so the word as drops out

parts.note: assizes were former county courts in England and Wales

explanation.surface: A ruling sorts out which law courts are surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The assizes were periodic criminal courts in England until 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things by dimension is to grade or classify them in this way.

clue.text: Upper garment in basin, also cap

parts.note: a tank is a basin or reservoir for liquid
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A garment found in a washbasin along with a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pullover worn over a shirt is an upper-body garment of this name.

clue.text: Busy person taking on board reorganisation of quiz game

indicators.note: taking on board means absorbing something inside

parts.note: a busy bee is a hard-working person

indicators.note: a reorganisation shuffles the letters of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A busy organiser takes on rearranging a quiz evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Bezique is a nineteenth-century card game; 'reorganisation of' scrambles the quiz letters to ZIQU and 'taking on board' encloses them in the insect, a byword for diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old card game for two players, played with a double pack.

clue.text: Figure manure must be spread, then left

indicators.note: spreading something disperses it, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction: manure must be spread, then you may leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening picture hides an anagram: 'must be spread' scatters the fertiliser letters into NUMERA, and 'then' simply leads to the abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure such as 7 or IV is a symbol standing for a number.

clue.text: Old record with new inset showing pop group's manager

parts.note: EP, an extended-play record, is an old format

indicators.note: new signals the word inset is made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vintage disc reissued with a new insert reveals a band manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns INSET into STEIN. Brian Epstein managed the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein was the famous manager of the Beatles, a pop group.
